sentences.zh: 顧和

translations.literal: Gu He
translations.idiomatic: Gu He

sentences.zh: 顧和，字君孝，侍中衆之族子也。

translations.literal: Gu He, courtesy name Junxiao, was a collateral descendant of Gu Zhong, who had served as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He, whose courtesy name was Junxiao, belonged to a cadet line of Gu Zhong, the former Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 曾祖容，吳荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong had been Inspector of Jing Province under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong had served Wu as regional inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 祖相，臨海太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiang had been Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiang had been governor of Linhai commandery.

sentences.zh: 和二歲喪父，總角便有清操，族叔榮雅重之，曰：「此吾家麒麟，興吾宗者，必此子也。

translations.literal: He lost his father at age two; even as a boy wearing his hair in tufts he showed pure conduct. His clansman uncle Rong held him in high esteem and said, “This is our family’s qilin; the one who will raise up our lineage must be this boy.”
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at two, he showed moral clarity while still a child. His uncle Rong thought the world of him and declared, “Here is our clan’s qilin—this boy will restore our house.”

sentences.zh: 」時宗人球亦有令聞，為州別駕，榮謂之曰：「卿速步，君孝超卿矣！」

translations.literal: At that time another clansman, Qiu, also had a fine reputation and served as Provincial Aide. Rong said to him, “You move fast, but Junxiao will outpace you!”
translations.idiomatic: Another kinsman named Qiu was already known as capable and held the post of provincial aide. Rong told him bluntly, “You may be quick on your feet, but Junxiao will leave you behind.”

sentences.zh: 王導為揚州，辟從事。

translations.literal: When Wang Dao governed Yang Province, he summoned Gu He as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, while heading Yang Province, recruited Gu He onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 月旦當朝，未入，停車門外。

translations.literal: On the monthly dawn audience he had not yet entered; he stopped his carriage outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the first court session of the month, before going in, he drew up his carriage outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 周顗遇之，和方擇虱，夷然不動。

translations.literal: Zhou Yi encountered him; Gu He was picking lice from his clothing and remained utterly unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi came upon him as he sat picking lice from his robe, perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 顗既過，顧指和心曰：「此中何所有？

translations.literal: After Yi had passed, he turned and pointed at Gu He’s chest, saying, “What is inside here?”
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yi walked past, he turned back, tapped Gu He’s breast, and asked, “What have you got in there?”

sentences.zh: 」和徐應曰：「此中最是難測地。

translations.literal: Gu He answered slowly, “This is exactly the place that is hardest to fathom.”
translations.idiomatic: Gu He replied calmly, “This is the spot no one can easily read.”

sentences.zh: 」顗入，謂導曰：「卿州吏中有一令僕才。

translations.literal: Yi entered and said to Dao, “Among your provincial clerks there is one with the talent of a chief minister.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi went in and told Wang Dao, “One of your provincial aides has the makings of a chief minister.”

sentences.zh: 」導亦以為然。

translations.literal: Dao likewise thought so.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao agreed.

sentences.zh: 和嘗詣導，導小極，對之疲睡。

translations.literal: Gu He once visited Dao; Dao was slightly unwell and fell asleep facing him.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to Wang Dao, the minister was mildly indisposed and dozed off in Gu He’s presence.

sentences.zh: 和欲叩會之，因謂同坐曰：「昔每聞族叔元公道葉贊中宗，保全江表。

translations.literal: Gu He wished to wake him and therefore said to those seated with him, “I have often heard how my clansman Uncle Yuanda assisted Emperor Zhongzong with his virtue and preserved the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He considered rousing him and remarked to the others, “We always heard my uncle Yuanda praise Emperor Zhongzong’s cooperation with him and how together they kept the south secure.”

sentences.zh: 體小不安，令人喘息。

translations.literal: When his body was slightly unwell, it made one catch one’s breath.”
translations.idiomatic: Even a slight indisposition in such a man was enough to take one’s breath away.”

sentences.zh: 」導覺之，謂和曰：「卿珪璋特達，機警有鋒，不徒東南之美，實為海內之俊。

translations.literal: Dao woke, heard him, and said to Gu He, “You stand apart like fine ritual jade—you are alert and incisive; you are not merely the finest of the southeast but truly eminent within the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao woke, overheard him, and said, “You are cut from exceptional stuff—sharp and perceptive. You are not only the best the southeast has to offer; you rank among the finest in the empire.”

sentences.zh: 」由是遂知名。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became known.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment his name was made.

sentences.zh: 既而導遣八部從事之部，和為下傳還，同時俱見，諸從事各言二千石官長得失，和獨無言。

translations.literal: Presently Dao sent out eight department aides on inspection tours; Gu He returned as courier from the lower districts and was received together with them. Each aide spoke of the merits and faults of the two-thousand-shi officials; Gu He alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Dao dispatched eight regional inspectors; Gu He came back from the outer circuits with their reports and was admitted with the rest. Every inspector aired complaints about the commandery governors—only Gu He stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 導問和：「卿何所聞？

translations.literal: Dao asked Gu He, “What have you heard?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao pressed him: “What did you hear?”

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「明公作輔，寧使網漏吞舟，何緣采聽風聞，以察察為政。

translations.literal: He answered, “You, sir, assist the throne—better that the net let great fish escape than that you heed rumor and govern by picky scrutiny.”
translations.idiomatic: Gu He replied, “You govern as chief minister—surely the net may let the great fish slip rather than you chase gossip and rule by nit-picking.”

sentences.zh: 」導咨嗟稱善。

translations.literal: Dao sighed with admiration and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sighed his approval.

sentences.zh: 累遷司徒左曹掾。

translations.literal: He rose through successive appointments to aide in the Left Bureau of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced step by step to secretary in the Minister of Education’s left section.

sentences.zh: 時東海王沖為長水校尉，妙選僚屬，以沛國劉耽為司馬，和為主簿。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Donghai, Chong, was Colonel of Changshui and chose his staff with care, appointing Liu Dan of Pei as marshal and Gu He as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: While the Prince of Donghai, Chong, held the colonelcy of the Changshui encampment, he handpicked his staff, naming Liu Dan of Pei marshal and Gu He chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，除司徒掾。

translations.literal: In the early Yongchang era he was appointed aide to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongchang reign he received appointment as secretary to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 太甯初，王敦請為主簿，遷太子舍人、車騎參軍、護軍長史。

translations.literal: In the early Taining era Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk; he was promoted to attendant of the heir apparent, army adviser to the chariot and cavalry general, and senior clerk to the Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taining, Wang Dun took him on as chief clerk; he rose to gentleman-attendant at the heir’s palace, then adviser on the staff of the chariot-and-cavalry general and chief clerk to the Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 王導為揚州，請為別駕，所歷皆著稱。

translations.literal: When Wang Dao governed Yang Province he invited him as Provincial Aide; in every post he earned acclaim.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao ran Yang Province he brought Gu He in as provincial aide; everywhere he served, people praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎侍郎、尚書吏部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman at the Palace Gate and Minister in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to gentleman of the palace gate and served in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 司空郗鑒請為長史，領晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jian requested him as senior clerk and concurrent Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian, minister of works, asked him to serve as chief clerk while doubling as prefect of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 咸康初，拜御史中丞，劾奏尚書左丞戴抗髒汙百萬，付法議罪，並免尚書傅玩、郎劉傭官，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: In the early Xiankang era he was appointed Palace Assistant Censor and impeached the Left Assistant Minister Dai Kang for corruption involving a million in cash, handing him to the judiciary for sentencing; he also secured dismissal for Minister Fu Wan and Gentleman Liu Yong—the hundred officials all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiankang he became imperial censor and charged Assistant Minister of the Left Dai Kang with embezzling a million cash, sending the case to the courts; Minister Fu Wan and Gentleman Liu Yong were stripped of office as well. The bureaucracy trembled at him.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，中興東遷，舊章多闕，而冕旒飾以翡翠珊瑚及雜珠等。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the restoration moved the court eastward, old regulations were largely missing, and the king’s crown pendants were ornamented with jadeite, coral, and miscellaneous pearls.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled east, many ritual codes were lost; even the twelve strings of the imperial crown had been decked out with jadeite, coral, and assorted beads.

sentences.zh: 和奏：「舊冕十有二旒，皆用玉珠，今用雜珠等，非禮。

translations.literal: Gu He memorialized: “The ancient crown had twelve pendants, all of jade beads; now miscellaneous pearls are used—this is contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He submitted: “The classical crown carries twelve tassels of jade beads. Substituting mixed pearls breaks the rites.”

sentences.zh: 若不能用玉，可用白旋珠。

translations.literal: If jade cannot be used, white spinel pearls may be used.”
translations.idiomatic: If true jade cannot be had, use white spinel pearls instead.”

sentences.zh: 」成帝於是始下太常改之。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng thereupon ordered the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng then instructed the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to correct it.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝以保母周氏有阿保之勞，欲假其名號，內外皆奉詔。

translations.literal: Previously the emperor had wished to grant a title to his nurse, Lady Zhou, for her nurturing care; everyone inside and outside the court obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor wanted to give his wet nurse, Lady Zhou, an honorific rank for raising him, and the whole court was prepared to go along.

sentences.zh: 和獨上疏以為「周保佑聖躬，不遺其勳，第舍供給擬于戚屬，恩澤所加已為過隆。

translations.literal: Gu He alone submitted a memorial arguing that “Lady Zhou had guarded the imperial person and her merit was not forgotten; her quarters and provisions already matched those of kin; the favor shown her was already excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He alone argued that Lady Zhou had cared for the sovereign and already received ample reward—housing and allowances fit for family—and that further honors would overshoot decency.

sentences.zh: 若假名號，記籍未見明比，惟漢靈帝以乳母趙嬈為平氏君，此末代之私恩，非先代之令典。

translations.literal: If a title were granted, the records offered no clear parallel except Emperor Ling of Han elevating his wet nurse Zhao Rao as Lady of Ping—that was private favor from a degenerate age, not a standard from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Granting her a formal title had no respectable precedent except Emperor Ling’s scandalous elevation of his nurse Zhao Rao—private indulgence from a fallen age, not a model worth following.

sentences.zh: 且君舉必書，將軌物垂則。

translations.literal: Moreover every deed of a ruler is recorded; it is meant to set patterns for things and hand down models.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, whatever a ruler does goes into the histories and becomes the pattern others must live by.

sentences.zh: 書而不法，後嗣何觀！

translations.literal: If it is recorded yet not lawful, what will posterity think!”
translations.idiomatic: Record something irregular, and what lesson does it teach those who come after!”

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書，頻徙領軍將軍、太常卿、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, then moved several times to General Who Guards the Army, Chamberlain for Ceremonial, and Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated into the Ministry of Personnel, then successively commanded the palace armies, headed the Chamberlain’s office, and served as libationer of the national university.

sentences.zh: 康帝即位，將祀南北郊，和議以為車駕宜親行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended the throne and was about to sacrifice at the southern and northern suburban altars, Gu He argued that the imperial carriage ought to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang planned suburban sacrifices north and south; Gu He insisted the emperor should attend in person.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，皆躬親行禮。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it and personally performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice and carried out every ritual himself.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，以母老固辭，詔書敕喻，物聽暮出朝還，其見優遇如此。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat but firmly declined on account of his mother’s age; an edict urged him on and allowed him to leave court at dusk and return at dawn—such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the secretariat, he begged off because his mother was elderly; the throne wrote to insist and let him go home at nightfall yet attend audiences at dawn—an extraordinary courtesy.

sentences.zh: 尋朝議以端右之副不宜處外，更拜銀青光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon court opinion held that the deputy of the chief minister should not serve outside; he was reassigned as Grand Master with Silver and Blue Ribbon and Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion soon decided the vice premier ought not hold an outside post, so he was made grand master of the palace with silver and blue ribbon while remaining libationer of the academy.

sentences.zh: 頃之，母憂去職，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Before long he left office for mourning over his mother and was famed for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned and earned a reputation for exemplary mourning.

sentences.zh: 既練，衛將軍褚裒上疏薦和，起為尚書令，遣散騎郎喻旨。

translations.literal: After the second-month ceremony, General Who Guards the Court Chu Pou memorialized to recommend Gu He and summon him as Director of the Imperial Secretariat; a gentleman of the palace gate was sent to convey the order.
translations.idiomatic: After the zhuan rites, Chu Pou, general who guards the court, recommended him for director of the secretariat and the court dispatched a palace messenger with the summons.

sentences.zh: 和每見逼促，輒號咷慟絕，謂所親曰：「古人或有釋其憂服以祗王命，蓋以才足干時，故不得不體國徇義。

translations.literal: Whenever Gu He was pressed, he would wail until he lost consciousness and said to those close to him, “Men of old sometimes set aside mourning garb to answer the king’s command because their talent met the needs of the age and they could not but put the state before personal duty.
translations.idiomatic: Each time officials pressured him, Gu He sobbed until he fainted and told his intimates, “Ancient worthies sometimes shed mourning to obey a summons when their abilities were indispensable—but I am less capable than most even in ordinary times.”

sentences.zh: 吾在常日猶不如人，況今中心荒亂，將何以補於萬分，只足以示輕忘孝道，貽素冠之義耳。

translations.literal: “How much less now, when my heart is in chaos—how could I supply even a fraction of what is needed? I would only show contempt for filial piety and betray the meaning of the plain cap.”
translations.idiomatic: “Now my mind is in ruins—what good could I do? I would only advertise disdain for mourning and shame the ideal of the unadorned cap.”

sentences.zh: 」帝又下詔曰：「百揆務殷，端右總要，而曠職經久，甚以悒然。

translations.literal: The emperor issued another edict: “The myriad duties are pressing and the chief minister’s post is vital, yet it has long stood empty—I am deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote again: “State business piles up and the director’s office is the hinge of government, yet it stands vacant—this weighs on me.”

sentences.zh: 昔先朝政道休明，中夏隆盛，山賈諸公皆釋服從時，不獲遂其情禮。

translations.literal: In former times, when government was enlightened and the Central Plain flourished, gentlemen such as Shan Tao still set aside mourning to follow the times and could not indulge private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Under earlier reigns, when the realm prospered, even men like Shan Tao put aside mourning to serve—they could not cling to private grief alone.

sentences.zh: 況今日艱難百王之弊，尚書令禮已過祥練，豈得聽不赴急疾而遂罔極之情乎！

translations.literal: How much more today amid the hardships and inherited ills of a hundred kings—the Director of the Secretariat has already passed the auspicious and practice periods—can he be allowed to heed boundless grief and ignore urgent need!”
translations.idiomatic: Today’s troubles pile higher still; you have already passed the extended mourning stages—can we let you hide in endless sorrow while the realm waits?”

sentences.zh: 」和表疏十餘上，遂不起，服闋，然後視職。

translations.literal: Gu He submitted more than ten memorials and would not rise; only after mourning ended did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He answered with over ten memorials refusing to serve; he reported for duty only after the mourning term closed.

sentences.zh: 時南中郎將謝尚領宣城內史，收涇令陳幹殺之，有司以尚違法糾黜，詔原之。

translations.literal: At that time the General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Xie Shang, concurrently administered Xuancheng interior commandery: he arrested and executed Magistrate Chen Gan of Jing. The authorities ruled that Shang had violated the law and should be dismissed; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang, leader of the southern household guards and acting prefect of Xuancheng, seized and executed Jing county magistrate Chen Gan. Officials wanted him cashiered for breaking statute, but an edict let him off.

sentences.zh: 和重奏曰：「尚先劾奸髒罪，入甲戍赦，聽自首減死。

translations.literal: Gu He submitted a further memorial: “Shang had earlier impeached Gan for corruption; the case fell under the Jiaxu amnesty, which allowed confession in exchange for commuting the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He fired back: “Xie Shang first denounced Chen Gan’s graft; the matter was covered by the Jiaxu amnesty, which permitted voluntary surrender to avoid execution.

sentences.zh: 而尚近表雲幹包藏奸猾，輒收行刑。

translations.literal: Yet Shang’s recent memorial claims Gan harbored treachery and so he seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xie Shang writes that Chen Gan was secretly malicious and therefore had to be arrested and killed.”

sentences.zh: 幹事狀自郡，非犯軍戎，不由都督。

translations.literal: Gan’s affair arose from the commandery; it did not involve military crime and did not pass through the area commander.
translations.idiomatic: The case belonged to the civil administration—it was no battlefield offense and never crossed the regional commander’s desk.”

sentences.zh: 案尚蒙親賢之舉，荷文武之任，不能為國惜體，平心聽斷，內挾小憾，肆其威虐，遠近怪愕，莫不解體。

translations.literal: Consider: Shang enjoys selection as a trusted worthy and bears civil and military responsibility; he could not safeguard the dignity of the state or judge impartially—instead he nursed a petty grudge and wantonly abused his power. Near and far were astonished; none failed to lose confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang was picked as a trusted elite with both civil and martial duty, yet he indulged a private spite and threw his weight around instead of protecting the law’s dignity; officials everywhere were dumbfounded and lost faith in him.

sentences.zh: 尚忝外屬，宥之有典，至於下吏，宜正刑辟。

translations.literal: Shang, though related to the empress dowager’s kin, may be forgiven under precedent; as for subordinate clerks, proper punishment should be applied.”
translations.idiomatic: Because he is imperial in-law, mercy may have precedent—but junior officers who abuse authority deserve the full penalty.”

sentences.zh: 」尚，皇太后舅，故寢其奏。

translations.literal: Shang was the empress dowager’s uncle, so the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang was the empress dowager’s uncle, so the throne quietly buried Gu He’s protest.

sentences.zh: 時汝南王統、江夏公衛崇並為庶母制服三年，和乃奏曰：「禮所以軌物成教，故有國家者莫不崇正明本，以一其統，斯人倫之紀，不二之道也。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Runan, Tong, and Duke of Jiangxia, Wei Chong, both observed three years’ mourning for a concubine mother. Gu He therefore memorialized: “Ritual exists to regulate conduct and complete instruction; therefore those who possess a state none fail to honor the correct root and unify the system—this is the norm of human relations and the single path that admits no doubling.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Tong of Runan and Duke Wei Chong of Jiangxia both wore three-year mourning for foster mothers, Gu He argued: “Rites govern behavior and teaching; every state affirms one legitimate lineage. That principle admits no split allegiance.

sentences.zh: 為人後者，降其所出，奪天屬之性，顯至公之義，降殺節文，著于周典。

translations.literal: Those who become heirs to another line demote their birth parents, strip natural affection in favor of supreme impartiality, and the graduated rules are set forth in the Zhou canon.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted heirs downgrade birth parents to serve the main line—the Zhou rituals spell out the gradations.”

sentences.zh: 案汝南王統為庶母居廬服重，江夏公衛崇本由疏屬，開國之緒，近喪所生，復行重制，違冒禮度，肆其私情。

translations.literal: Consider: the Prince of Runan wears deep mourning in a hut for a concubine mother; Duke Wei Chong, born from a distant branch, owes his noble fief to the founding line, yet having lately buried his birth mother he again observes heavy mourning—violating ritual bounds and indulging private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong keeps full mourning for a concubine; Duke Wei, a distant cadet ennobled only by the founding ancestor, buries his natural mother and then insists on the heaviest rites—flouting protocol for private sentiment.

sentences.zh: 閭閻許其過厚，談者莫以為非，則政道陵遲由乎禮廢，憲章頹替始于容違。

translations.literal: If commoners praise their excessive devotion and critics say nothing is wrong, then government declines because ritual collapses, and statutes crumble because indulgence is tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: If neighbors call it devotion and no one objects, governance slides because rites erode and law frays where exceptions multiply.

sentences.zh: 若弗糾正，無以齊物。

translations.literal: If this is not corrected, there is no way to standardize conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we correct this, we cannot hold everyone to one standard.

sentences.zh: 皆可下太常奪服。

translations.literal: All may be ordered through the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to strip the mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Send them all to the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to remove the improper mourning.

sentences.zh: 若不祗王命，應加貶黜。

translations.literal: If they disobey the royal command, demotion should be added.”
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who defies the decree should be degraded.”

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 和居任多所獻納，雖權臣不苟阿撓。

translations.literal: In office Gu He offered many remonstrances and recommendations; even toward powerful ministers he would not cringe or yield.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his tenure he spoke plainly to the throne and refused to truckle to mighty favorites.

sentences.zh: 和以疾篤辭位，拜左光祿大夫、儀同三司，加散騎常侍，尚書令如故。

translations.literal: Because Gu He’s illness was grave he resigned office; he was appointed Grand Master of the Left, Unequaled in Honor, concurrently Gentleman at the Palace Gate, while retaining his post as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When grave illness forced Gu He to yield his offices, the court still named him grand master of the left with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, added gentleman at the palace gate, and allowed him to remain director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: That same year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、司空，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; his posthumous name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named palace attendant and minister of works with the epithet Mu, meaning Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子淳，歷尚書吏部郎、給事黃門侍郎、左衛將軍。

translations.literal: His son Chun served as Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel, Gentleman for Palace Presentation at the Yellow Gate, and General Who Guards the Left.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu Chun rose through personnel posts, the yellow-gate palace corps, and command of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 袁瑰

translations.literal: Yuan Mei
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mei

sentences.zh: 袁瑰，字山甫，陳郡陽夏人，魏郎中令渙之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Mei, courtesy name Shanfu, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery and great-grandson of Yuan Huan, who had been Director of Gentlemen under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mei, courtesy Shanfu, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery and traced his descent from Yuan Huan, minister of gentlemen under Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖、父並早卒。

translations.literal: His grandfather and father both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Both his grandfather and father died early.

sentences.zh: 瑰與弟猷欲奉母避亂，求為江淮間縣，拜呂令，轉江都，因南渡。

translations.literal: Mei and his younger brother You wished to escort their mother away from turmoil and sought appointment to a county between the Yangzi and Huai; he was appointed magistrate of Lü, then transferred to Jiangdu, and thus crossed south.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brother You sought a riverside county post so they could move their mother out of chaos—first magistrate of Lü, then Jiangdu—and crossed south with her.

sentences.zh: 元帝以為丹陽令。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him prefect of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 中興建，拜奉朝請，遷治書御史。

translations.literal: When the restoration was founded he was appointed Court Presenter and promoted to palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern court was established he became court presenter and then imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 時東海王越屍既為石勒所焚，妃裴氏求招魂葬越，朝廷疑之。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Donghai, Yue, had already had his corpse burned by Shi Le; his consort Lady Pei sought to summon his soul for burial, and the court was uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Donghai’s body had been cremated by Shi Le; Lady Pei asked to bury a soul-summoning garment in lieu of remains, and ministers hesitated.

sentences.zh: 瑰與博士傅純議，以為招魂葬是謂埋神，不可從也。

translations.literal: Mei debated with Erudite Fu Chun and argued that soul-summoning burial meant burying the spirit and could not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mei and scholar Fu Chun argued that “summoning the soul” amounted to burying a ghost-soul and must be refused.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，雖許裴氏招魂葬越，遂下詔禁之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; although he allowed Lady Pei’s soul burial for Yue, he then issued an edict forbidding the practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted in principle yet let Lady Pei bury Prince Yue’s effigy, then banned the custom by edict.

sentences.zh: 尋除廬江太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became prefect of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王敦引為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Dun brought him in as adviser on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun took him on as consulting adviser.

sentences.zh: 俄為臨川太守。

translations.literal: Before long he was Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon transferred to Linchuan prefect.

sentences.zh: 敦平，為鎮南將軍陶侃軍司。

translations.literal: After Dun was crushed he served as army marshal to General Who Guards the South Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Dun was defeated, Yuan Mei became army marshal on Tao Kan’s staff in the southern command.

sentences.zh: 尋自解還都，游於會稽。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned on his own initiative and returned to the capital, then traveled in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and came back to Jiankang, then wandered in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之難，與王舒共起義軍，以功封長合鄉侯，征補散騎常侍，徙大司農尋除國子祭酒。

translations.literal: During Su Jun’s rebellion he raised troops with Wang Shu; for merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changhe, summoned as Gentleman at the Palace Gate, transferred to Minister of Agriculture, and soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rebelled he mustered forces with Wang Shu, earned a village marquisate at Changhe, returned to court as gentleman at the palace gate, moved to minister of agriculture, and shortly became libationer of the academy.

sentences.zh: 頃之，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally Gentleman at the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon picked up a concurrent post as gentleman at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 于時喪亂之後，禮教陵遲，瑰上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time, after deaths and turmoil, ritual teaching had declined; Mei submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: With the realm broken and etiquette in ruins, Yuan Mei addressed the throne:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，成帝從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Cheng accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 國學之興，自瑰始也。

translations.literal: The revival of the national academy began with Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The national university owed its revival to Yuan Mei.

sentences.zh: 以年在懸車，上疏告老，尋卒，追贈光祿大夫，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Because his years had reached the age for retiring (“suspended carriage”), he memorialized to retire; soon afterward he died and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Past the conventional retirement age he asked leave to retire, died soon after, and received posthumous honors as grand master of brilliant splendor with the canonizing epithet Gong.

sentences.zh: 子喬嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qiao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Qiao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子喬

translations.literal: Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao.

sentences.zh: 子喬

translations.literal: Son Qiao
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao

sentences.zh: 喬字彥叔。

translations.literal: Qiao’s courtesy name was Yanshu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao’s courtesy name was Yanshu.

sentences.zh: 初拜佐著作郎。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed editorial aide.
translations.idiomatic: He began as assistant editor in the institute.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍桓溫請為司馬，除司徒左西屬，不就，拜尚書郎。

translations.literal: General Who Supports the State Huan Wen requested him as marshal; he was appointed western aide on the left of the Minister of Education but declined; he was appointed Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen tried to hire him as marshal; the court named him western aide under the minister of education—he refused—and then gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 桓溫鎮京口，復引為司馬，領廣陵相。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen garrisoned Jingkou he again brought Yuan Qiao in as marshal and concurrent Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, stationed at Jingkou, recalled Yuan Qiao as his marshal and put him in charge of Guangling as well.

sentences.zh: 初，喬與褚裒友善，及康獻皇后臨朝，喬與裒書曰：「皇太后踐登正阼，臨御皇朝，將軍之于國，外姓之太上皇也。

translations.literal: Earlier Qiao had been friendly with Chu Pou. When Empress Dowager Kangxian held court, Qiao wrote to Pou: “The empress dowager has ascended the legitimate throne and rules the dynasty; for you, General, in relation to the state, you are like a senior emperor by marriage though not of the imperial surname.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao had long been close to Chu Pou. Once Empress Dowager Kangxian began regency, he wrote: “The queen mother sits on the proper throne and governs the realm—you are to this court what a paramount father-in-law would be to an outsider clan.”

sentences.zh: 至於皇子近屬，咸有揖讓之禮，而況策名人臣，而交媟人父，天性攸尊，亦宜體國而重矣。

translations.literal: Even imperial princes and close kin observe yielding courtesy—how much more one who bears ministerial rank on the roster yet behaves toward another man’s father with improper familiarity? Nature sets whom we must honor; you too should weigh the state above private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Even imperial kin still observe deference in public—how much more a minister listed in the roster who would bandy intimacies with another man’s father? Natural obligations of respect exist; you should put the polity first.

sentences.zh: 故友之好，請於此辭。

translations.literal: Therefore I ask to end our old friendship here.
translations.idiomatic: So I must end our former friendship at this point.

sentences.zh: 染絲之變，墨翟致懷，岐路之感，楊硃興歎，況于將軍游處少長，雖世譽先後而臭味同歸也。

translations.literal: The dyeing of silk moved Mozi; the fork in the road made Yang Zhu sigh—how much more we who have grown up together: though the world praised us in different order, our temperaments belong to the same track.
translations.idiomatic: Mozi mourned how silk changes color in the dye; Yang Zhu wept at life’s diverging roads—so too for us, friends since youth: fame may come sooner or later, but we breathed the same air.

sentences.zh: 平昔之交，與禮數而降，箕踞之歎，隨時事而替，雖欲虛詠濠肆，脫落儀制，其能得乎！

translations.literal: Plain friendship must yield to ritual gradations; the lounging reproach changes with events—how could we still babble of Zhuangzi’s riverside freedom and cast off formalities?
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy now narrows what old camaraderie allowed; the reproof for sprawling discourtesy shifts with the times—there is no going back to abstract chatter about Carefree Roaming and shedding ritual.

sentences.zh: 來物無停，變化遷代，豈惟寸晷，事亦有之。

translations.literal: Coming things never pause; change and succession roll on—not only in brief moments; affairs do the same.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing stays still; times turn over faster than a shadow—circumstances move too.

sentences.zh: 夫禦器者神，制衆以約，願將軍貽情無事，以理勝為任，親杖賢達，以納善為大。

translations.literal: He who steers the vessel must be spirit-like; he who rules the many must keep restraint. I hope you will set emotion aside while affairs are calm, take defeating chaos as your task, lean on worthy men, and make welcoming good counsel your chief aim.
translations.idiomatic: The pilot must be nimble; governing crowds demands simplicity—please quiet personal feeling while things are still, make order your burden, draw near to the wise, and prize sound advice above all.

sentences.zh: 執筆惆悵，不能自盡。

translations.literal: Holding the brush I am melancholy and cannot fully express myself.
translations.idiomatic: Pen in hand, I am heavy-hearted and cannot say all I mean.

sentences.zh: 」論者以為得禮。

translations.literal: Commentators held that he had understood ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that he had struck the proper ritual note.

sentences.zh: 遷安西諮議參軍、長沙相，不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to adviser on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the West and Chancellor of Changsha but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: They moved him to adviser under the general pacifying the west and offered him Changsha—he declined both.

sentences.zh: 尋督沔中諸戍江夏隨義陽三郡軍事、建武將軍、江夏相。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised military affairs of the garrisons along the Han and the three commanderies Jiangxia, Sui, and Yiyang, served as General Who Establishes Might, and was Chancellor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded Han River defenses plus Jiangxia, Sui, and Yiyang as General Who Establishes Might and prefect of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 時桓溫謀伐蜀，衆以為不可，喬勸溫曰：「夫經略大事，故非常情所具，智者了于胸心，然後舉無遺算耳。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Wen planned to attack Shu; most thought it impossible. Qiao urged Wen: “Grand strategy is not what ordinary minds grasp—only after a wise man has settled it in his breast does an undertaking leave nothing unplanned.”
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen aimed at Shu, court opinion scoffed. Yuan Qiao told him, “Great campaigns exceed common sense—only when a strategist has done the math in silence does the plan hold.”

sentences.zh: 今天下之難，二寇而已。

translations.literal: The peril facing the realm today is only two bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The empire today faces just two enemies.

sentences.zh: 蜀雖險固，方胡為弱，將欲除之，先從易者。

translations.literal: Shu is rugged, but compared with the Hu it is the weaker; if you intend to eliminate them, begin with the easier.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is steep but weaker than the northern tribes—cut the weak link first.

sentences.zh: 今溯流萬里，經歷天險，彼或有備，不必可克。

translations.literal: Attacking upriver ten thousand li through heaven’s narrows, they may be prepared and victory is not assured.
translations.idiomatic: A river assault ten thousand li upstream runs every natural hazard—the enemy may be ready, so success is no certainty.

sentences.zh: 然蜀人自以鬥絕一方，恃其完固，不修攻戰之具，若以精卒一萬，輕軍速進，比彼聞之，我已入其險要，李勢君臣不過自力一戰，擒之必矣。

translations.literal: Yet the Shu people pride themselves on isolation, trust their fortifications, and neglect weapons; if with ten thousand picked troops you march fast and light, by the time word reaches them you will already hold the choke points—Li Shi’s court can manage only one desperate battle; capture is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Shu rests smug behind its walls and lets its arms rust—strike with ten thousand elites before rumor catches up, seize the narrows, and Li Shi’s regime will manage one frantic fight at best; victory follows.

sentences.zh: 論者恐大軍既西，胡必窺覦，此又似是而非。

translations.literal: Critics fear that once the main army goes west the Hu will spy an opening—this sounds plausible yet is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Critics warn that marching west invites Hu raids—it sounds sensible but is not.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 胡聞萬里片征伐，以為內有重備，必不敢動。

translations.literal: When the Hu hear that a campaign ten thousand li away is underway, they assume heavy interior defenses and will not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Northern tribes hearing of an expedition far away conclude the interior is heavily guarded and hesitate to move.

sentences.zh: 縱復越逸江渚，諸軍足以守境，此無憂矣。

translations.literal: Even if raiders slip across the Yangzi, our garrisons suffice to hold the frontier—there is no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Should raiders ford the Yangzi anyway, frontier armies can contain them—there is little to fear.

sentences.zh: 蜀土富實，號稱天府，昔諸葛武侯欲以抗衡中國。

translations.literal: Shu’s soil is rich and famed as heaven’s storehouse; once Zhuge Liang meant to rival the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is fertile—Zhuge Liang once meant to use it to challenge the heartland.

sentences.zh: 今誠不能為害，然勢據上流，易為寇盜。

translations.literal: Today it truly cannot harm us, yet sitting upstream it easily breeds banditry.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot hurt us much now, yet perched upstream it invites marauders.

sentences.zh: 若襲而取之者，有其人衆，此國之大利也。

translations.literal: If we seize it we gain its population—that is the realm’s great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Taking it yields manpower—a major prize for the state.

sentences.zh: 」溫從之，使喬以江夏相領二千人為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Wen accepted this and ordered Qiao, as Chancellor of Jiangxia, to lead two thousand men as the army’s spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen agreed and gave Yuan Qiao two thousand Jiangxia troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 師次彭模，去賊已近，議者欲兩道並進，以分賊勢。

translations.literal: The army halted at Pengmo; the enemy was near. Advisers wished to advance along two routes to split enemy strength.
translations.idiomatic: They camped at Pengmo with the foe close by; staff urged a two-pronged advance to divide Shu forces.

sentences.zh: 喬曰：「今深入萬里，置之死地，士無反顧之心，所謂人自為戰者也。

translations.literal: Qiao said: “Now we have plunged ten thousand li and placed the army on deadly ground; the men have no thought of turning back—each fights as if for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao replied, “We are ten thousand li deep on fatal terrain—soldiers fight as if their lives depend on each stroke.”

sentences.zh: 今分為兩軍，軍力不一，萬一偏敗，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: If we split into two armies with uneven strength, should one wing fail the whole enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Split the force and uneven odds mean one defeat loses everything.

sentences.zh: 不如全軍而進，棄去釜甑，齎三日糧，勝可必矣。

translations.literal: Better advance with the whole army, cast aside cooking pots, carry three days’ grain—then victory is assured.
translations.idiomatic: Better drive forward intact, smash the cauldrons, march with three days’ rations—then we cannot lose.

sentences.zh: 」溫以為然，即一時俱進。

translations.literal: Wen agreed and advanced all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen concurred and pushed everyone forward together.

sentences.zh: 去成都十里，與賊大戰，前鋒失利，喬軍亦退，矢及馬首，左右失色。

translations.literal: Ten li from Chengdu they fought a great battle; the vanguard faltered, Qiao’s line fell back, arrows reached his horse’s head, and his attendants blanched.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li short of Chengdu the great clash came—the van broke, Yuan Qiao’s men wavered, bolts whipped his mount’s mane, and aides turned pale.

sentences.zh: 喬因麾而進，聲氣愈厲，遂大破之，長驅至成都。

translations.literal: Qiao waved the army onward; his voice grew fiercer; they routed the enemy and drove straight to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao signaled the advance, shouted louder, shattered the Shu host, and raced to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 李勢既降，勢將鄧定、隗文以其屬反，衆各萬餘。

translations.literal: After Li Shi surrendered, his generals Deng Ding and Kui Wen rebelled with their commands, each over ten thousand strong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Shi yielded, generals Deng Ding and Kui Wen revolted with ten thousand men apiece.

sentences.zh: 溫自擊定，喬擊文，破之。

translations.literal: Wen personally attacked Ding while Qiao attacked Wen and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen took Deng Ding himself; Yuan Qiao crushed Kui Wen.

sentences.zh: 進號龍驤將軍，封湘西伯。

translations.literal: Qiao’s rank rose to General Who Soars like the Dragon; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to dragon-soaring general and made baron of Xiangxi.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年三十六，溫甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: Soon he died at age thirty-six; Wen deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after at thirty-six; Huan Wen grieved bitterly.

sentences.zh: 追贈益州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Inspector of Yi Province with the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him inspector of Yi with the epithet Jian, meaning Simple.

sentences.zh: 喬博學有文才，注《論語》及《詩》，並諸文筆皆行於世。

translations.literal: Qiao was broadly learned and literary; he annotated the Analects and the Odes, and his essays circulated widely.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao was learned and wrote well—his glosses on the Analects and the Odes plus his essays stayed in circulation.

sentences.zh: 子方平嗣，亦以軌素自立，辟大司馬掾，歷義興、琅邪太守。

translations.literal: His son Fangping inherited; he too upheld plain integrity, was summoned as aide to the grand marshal, and served as Administrator of Yixing and Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fangping succeeded, kept a sober household, joined the grand marshal’s staff, and governed Yixing and Langye.

sentences.zh: 卒，子山松嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Shansong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Shansong inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 喬孫山松

translations.literal: Grandson Shansong
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shansong, Qiao’s grandson

sentences.zh: 喬孫山松

translations.literal: Grandson Shansong
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shansong

sentences.zh: 山松少有才名，博學有文章，著《後漢書》百篇。

translations.literal: Shansong in youth had a talented name; he was learned and wrote well, composing a hundred-chapter Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Shansong was celebrated young—learned, prolific, author of a hundred-chapter Later Han history.

sentences.zh: 衿情秀遠，善音樂。

translations.literal: His temperament was refined and remote; he excelled at music.
translations.idiomatic: He carried an aloof grace and loved music.

sentences.zh: 舊歌有《行路難》曲，辭頗疏質，山松好之，乃文其辭句，婉其節制，每因酣醉縱歌之。

translations.literal: An old ballad had the tune “Hard Road”; its words were rough. Shansong loved it, polished the lyrics, smoothed the rhythm, and whenever drunk would sing it wildly.
translations.idiomatic: The old song “Hard Road” had crude words; Shansong refined the verse and meter, then belted it whenever wine flowed.

sentences.zh: 聽者莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Listeners invariably wept.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners wept every time.

sentences.zh: 初羊曇善唱樂，桓伊能輓歌，及山松《行路難》繼之，時人謂之「三絕」。

translations.literal: Once Yang Tan sang well and Huan Yi could sing laments; Shansong’s “Hard Road” followed—people of the time called them the “three unmatched talents.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tan sang beautifully, Huan Yi mastered dirges, then Shansong’s “Hard Road”—contemporaries dubbed them the three incomparables.

sentences.zh: 時張湛好於齋前種松柏，而山松每出遊，好令左右作輓歌，人謂「湛屋下陳屍，山松道上行殯。」

translations.literal: Zhang Zhan liked planting pines and cypress before his study; whenever Shansong went out he had attendants perform lambsongs—people said “Corpses laid out under Zhan’s roof; funeral processions march wherever Shansong rides.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhan grew pines and cypress by his study; Shansong paraded with hired mourners—wags said, “Zhan stacks corpses at home while Shansong holds street funerals.”

sentences.zh: 山松歷顯位，為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Shansong rose to eminent posts and became Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to high office and governed Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫恩作亂，山松守滬瀆，城陷被害。

translations.literal: When Sun En rebelled, Shansong defended Hudu; the city fell and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En’s revolt caught him defending Hudu—the city fell and he died.

sentences.zh: 瑰弟猷

translations.literal: Mei’s younger brother You.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan You, Mei’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 瑰弟猷

translations.literal: Mei’s younger brother You.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan You.

sentences.zh: 猷字申甫，少與瑰齊名。

translations.literal: You, courtesy name Shenfu, in youth shared Mei’s reputation.
translations.idiomatic: You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and was as celebrated as his elder brother in youth.

sentences.zh: 代瑰為呂令，復相繼為江都，由是俱渡江。

translations.literal: He succeeded Mei as magistrate of Lü and afterward likewise served Jiangdu; thus both crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Mei as prefect of Lü, then Jiangdu in turn, and crossed south with him.

sentences.zh: 瑰為丹陽，猷為武康，兄弟列宰名邑，論者美之。

translations.literal: Mei governed Danyang and You Wukang; as brothers they administered famed counties together—critics praised them.
translations.idiomatic: While Mei ran Danyang, You governed Wukang—brothers holding celebrated seats together won admiration.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He rose through Palace Attendant and Chamberlain of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to palace attendant and minister of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 猷孫宏，見《文苑傳》。

translations.literal: You’s grandson Hong appears in the “Literary Men” biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yuan Hong is treated in the Literary Men section.

sentences.zh: 從祖準

translations.literal: Collateral ancestor Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhun, collateral great-uncle.

sentences.zh: 從祖準

translations.literal: Collateral ancestor Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhun.

sentences.zh: 準字孝尼，以儒學知名，注《喪服經》。

translations.literal: Zhun, courtesy name Xiaoni, was famed for Confucian scholarship and annotated the Scripture on Mourning Garb.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun, courtesy Xiaoni, earned renown as a classicist and wrote a commentary on mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 官至給事中。

translations.literal: His highest office was palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: He capped his career as palace aide.

sentences.zh: 準子沖，字景玄，光祿勳。

translations.literal: Zhun’s son Chong, courtesy name Jingxuan, served as Minister of Brilliant Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong, courtesy Jingxuan, rose to minister of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 沖子耽。

translations.literal: Chong’s son Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Chong’s heir was Dan.

sentences.zh: 準孫耽

translations.literal: Zhun’s grandson Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dan, grandson of Zhun.

sentences.zh: 準孫耽

translations.literal: Zhun’s grandson Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dan.

sentences.zh: 耽字彥道，少有才氣，倜儻不羈，為士類所稱。

translations.literal: Dan, courtesy name Yandao, showed youthful brilliance and unruly dash and won praise among gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, courtesy Yandao, had flair and swagger from youth and impressed the elite.

sentences.zh: 桓溫少時游於博徒，資產俱盡，尚有負進，思自振之方，莫知所出，欲求濟於耽，而耽在艱，試以告焉。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen was young he gambled until his assets were gone yet still owed debts; he sought a way to recover but knew none and wished to ask Dan for aid—Dan was in mourning but Wen tentatively told him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Huan Wen gambled away his fortune and still owed money; desperate for rescue yet unsure how, he approached Dan—who was observing mourning—but tested the waters anyway.

sentences.zh: 耽略無難色，遂變服懷布帽，隨溫與債主戲。

translations.literal: Dan showed no reluctance; he changed clothes, tucked a cloth cap under his arm, and followed Wen to game with the creditor.
translations.idiomatic: Dan agreed without hesitation—changed clothes, hid a cloth cap under his jacket, and joined Huan Wen at the creditor’s table.

sentences.zh: 耽素有藝名，債者聞之而不相識，謂之曰：「卿當不辦作袁彥道也。

translations.literal: Dan had long been famed for gaming skill; the creditor heard but did not recognize him and said, “You surely cannot play the part of Yuan Yandao.”
translations.idiomatic: Dan was legendary at dice; the creditor had heard the name but did not know his face and sneered, “You cannot possibly be Yuan Yandao.”

sentences.zh: 」遂就局十萬一擲，直上百萬。

translations.literal: They then joined the game with one hundred thousand wagered per throw, climbing straight to a million.
translations.idiomatic: They opened play at a hundred thousand cash per cast—stakes shot toward a million.

sentences.zh: 耽投馬絕叫，探布帽擲地，曰：「竟識袁彥道不？

translations.literal: Dan cast the horses with a shout, pulled out the cloth cap and threw it down, saying, “Do you recognize Yuan Yandao now?”
translations.idiomatic: Dan slammed his pieces down, hurled the cap to the floor, and roared, “Still doubt Yuan Yandao?”

sentences.zh: 」其通脫若此。

translations.literal: His unconventionality was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his swaggering nerve.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之役，王導引為參軍，隨導在石頭。

translations.literal: During Su Jun’s rising Wang Dao brought him in as army adviser and followed Dao at Stone Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: In Su Jun’s coup Wang Dao enlisted him as adviser and kept him at Stone fortress.

sentences.zh: 初，路永、匡術、寧等皆峻心腹，聞祖約奔敗，懼事不立，迭說峻誅大臣。

translations.literal: Earlier Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, Ning, and others had all been Su Jun’s trusted men; hearing Zu Yue had fled in defeat they feared the venture would fail and urged Jun repeatedly to execute great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, Ning, and company had been Su Jun’s inner circle; when Zu Yue collapsed they feared the plot would unravel and pressed Su Jun to purge senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 峻既不納，永等慮必敗，陰結於導。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen; Yong and company anticipated certain defeat and secretly allied with Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun refused; Yong’s faction foresaw doom and secretly negotiated with Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 導使耽潛說路永，使歸順。

translations.literal: Dao sent Dan secretly to persuade Yong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao had Dan approach Lu Yong quietly to defect.

sentences.zh: 峻平，封秭歸男，拜建威將軍、曆陽太守。

translations.literal: After Jun was crushed Dan was enfeoffed as Baron of Zigui, appointed General Who Establishes Might, and Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun fell, Dan earned the Zigui barony, generalship who establishes might, and Liyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸康初，石季龍游騎十餘匹至曆陽，耽上列不言騎少。

translations.literal: In the early Xiankang era Shi Jilong’s scouting riders—little more than a dozen horses—reached Liyang; Dan’s memorial listed them without mentioning how few they were.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiankang a handful of Shi Hu’s scouts appeared at Liyang; Dan’s report omitted how tiny the enemy band was.

sentences.zh: 時胡寇強盛，朝野危懼，王導以宰輔之重請自討之。

translations.literal: At that time Hu raiders were strong and court and countryside trembled; Wang Dao in his weight as chief minister requested permission to campaign personally.
translations.idiomatic: Northern pressure terrified everyone; chief minister Wang Dao volunteered to lead the response.

sentences.zh: 既而賊騎不多，又已退散，導止不行。

translations.literal: Presently it proved there were few enemy riders and they had dispersed; Dao halted and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon there proved to be almost no raiders—they had melted away—so Wang Dao stayed home.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以耽失於輕妄，黜之。

translations.literal: The court deemed Dan rash and reckless and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court cashiered Dan for reckless alarmism.

sentences.zh: 尋復為導從事中郎，方加大任，會卒，時年二十五。

translations.literal: Soon he again served Dao as attendant gentleman-in-chief; high office was about to come when he died at age twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Wang Dao’s senior attendant on the verge of promotion but died at twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 子質。

translations.literal: Son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 耽子質

translations.literal: Dan’s son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhi, Dan’s son.

sentences.zh: 耽子質

translations.literal: Dan’s son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質字道和。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Daohe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi bore the courtesy name Daohe.

sentences.zh: 自渙至質五世，並以道素繼業，惟其父耽以雄豪著。

translations.literal: From Huan down to Zhi for five generations all upheld plain moral continuity; only his father Dan was famed for brash heroism.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations from Yuan Huan through Zhi maintained sober virtue—only Dan stood out for swagger.

sentences.zh: 及質又以孝行稱。

translations.literal: When it came to Zhi he was also praised for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi himself earned renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 官歷琅邪內史、東陽太守。

translations.literal: He served as Interior Minister of Langye and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Langye interior commandery and Dongyang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 質子湛。

translations.literal: Zhi’s son Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: His heir was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 質子湛

translations.literal: Zhi’s son Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhan, Zhi’s son.

sentences.zh: 質子湛

translations.literal: Zhi’s son Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛字士深。

translations.literal: Zhan, courtesy name Shishen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan used the courtesy name Shishen.

sentences.zh: 少有操植，以沖粹自立，而無文華，故不為流俗所重。

translations.literal: From youth he held moral discipline and cultivated quiet purity without literary ornament, so vulgar taste did not esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he cultivated restraint and sober virtue rather than polish, so fashionable circles overlooked him.

sentences.zh: 時謝混為僕射，范泰贈湛及混詩云：「亦有後出雋，離群頗騫翥。

translations.literal: When Xie Hun was vice director Fan Tai presented Zhan and Hun a poem saying, “There are also late-coming talents who soar apart from the flock.”
translations.idiomatic: While Xie Hun served as vice director Fan Tai gifted them verse praising “later luminaries who rise above the herd.”

sentences.zh: 」湛恨而不答。

translations.literal: Zhan resented it and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan took offense and stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 自中書令為僕射、左光祿大夫、晉甯男，卒於官。

translations.literal: From Palace Commandant he became vice director, Grand Master of the Left, and Baron of Jinning; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from palace director to vice director, grand master of the left, and baron of Jinning—dying in harness.

sentences.zh: 湛弟豹。

translations.literal: Zhan’s younger brother Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Bao.

sentences.zh: 湛弟豹

translations.literal: Zhan’s younger brother Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bao, brother of Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛弟豹

translations.literal: Zhan’s younger brother Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bao.

sentences.zh: 豹字士蔚，博學善文辭，有經國材，為劉裕所知。

translations.literal: Bao, courtesy name Shiwei, was broadly learned and skilled at prose, possessed talent for governing the state, and came to Liu Yu’s attention.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bao, courtesy Shiwei, wrote well, knew the classics, showed administrative gifts, and impressed Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 後為太尉長史、丹陽尹，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as senior clerk to the grand commandant and Prefect of Danyang; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief of staff to the grand commandant and governor of Danyang, then died in office.

sentences.zh: 江逌

translations.literal: Jiang You
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You

sentences.zh: 江逌，字道載，陳留圉人也。

translations.literal: Jiang You, courtesy name Daozai, was a native of Yu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You, courtesy Daozai, came from Yu county in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖蕤，譙郡太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rui had been Administrator of Qiao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jiang Rui governed Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖允，蕪湖令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun had been magistrate of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun had been Wuhu county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 父濟，安東參軍。

translations.literal: His father Ji had been army adviser to the general pacifying the east.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served on the staff of the eastern pacification general.

sentences.zh: 逌少孤，與從弟灌共居，甚相友悌，由是獲當時之譽。

translations.literal: You was orphaned young and lived with his cousin Guan; they were devoted brothers and thereby won contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he lived with cousin Jiang Guan in harmony and earned a reputation for fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 避蘇峻之亂，屏居臨海，絕棄人事，翦茅結宇，耽玩載籍，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Fleeing Su Jun’s turmoil he withdrew to Linhai, cut himself off from worldly affairs, thatched a hut, reveled in books, and resolved to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun threw the realm into chaos he withdrew to Linhai, shut out politics, built a thatched study, buried himself in texts, and meant to finish his life there.

sentences.zh: 本州辟從事，除佐著作郎，並不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as aide and he was appointed editorial aide—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: The province tried to hire him as aide and the court named him editorial assistant—he refused both.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍蔡謨命為參軍，何充復引為驃騎功曹。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Cai Mo appointed him army adviser; He Chong again brought him in as merit clerk for the chariot-and-cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo took him as military adviser; He Chong later added him as merit clerk on the cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 以家貧，求試守，為太末令。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor he sought probationary appointment and became magistrate of Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by poverty he sought an acting post and became magistrate of Taiwei.

sentences.zh: 縣界深山中，有亡命數百家，恃險為阻，前後守宰莫能平。

translations.literal: Deep in the county mountains several hundred fugitives relied on rough terrain; successive magistrates could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of outlaws held the mountain fastnesses—prefect after prefect failed to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 逌到官，召其魁帥，厚加撫接，諭以禍福，旬月之間，繈負而至，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: When You arrived he summoned their chiefs, treated them generously, explained fortune and peril, and within a month they came carrying children on their backs—the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: You called in the bandit leaders, treated them generously, explained consequences, and within weeks families surrendered on his doorstep—the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 州檄為治中，轉別駕，遷吳令。

translations.literal: The province ordered him administrator of records, then transferred him to provincial aide, then promoted him magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from provincial clerk to aide and then prefect of Wu county.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍殷浩將謀北伐，請為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: General of the Central Army Yin Hao planned a northern expedition and requested You as adviser on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao prepared to march north he asked You to join his staff as adviser.

sentences.zh: 浩甚重之，遷長史。

translations.literal: Hao esteemed him highly and promoted him to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao valued him and moved him up to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 浩方修復洛陽，經營荒梗，逌為上佐，甚有匡弼之益，軍中書檄皆以委逌。

translations.literal: As Hao restored Luoyang and worked the ruined wastes, You as chief aide offered strong corrective benefit; military orders and proclamations were all entrusted to You.
translations.idiomatic: While Yin Hao rebuilt Luoyang from ruins You served as chief clerk with decisive help—every order and dispatch passed through him.

sentences.zh: 時羌及丁零叛，浩軍震懼。

translations.literal: At that time Qiang and Dingling tribes rebelled and Hao’s army trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang and Dingling auxiliaries mutinied Yin Hao’s army panicked.

sentences.zh: 姚襄去浩十里結營以逼浩，浩令逌擊之。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang camped ten li from Hao to pressure him; Hao ordered You to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang pitched camp ten li away to pin Yin Hao; Hao sent You to attack.

sentences.zh: 逌進兵至襄營，謂將校曰：「今兵非不精，而衆少於羌，且其塹柵甚固，難與校力，吾當以計破之。

translations.literal: Jiang You advanced his troops to Yao Xiang’s camp and told the officers: “Our troops are not unfit, but we are fewer than the Qiang and their ditches and palisades are strong—hard to match strength head-on; I shall defeat them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You advanced on Yao Xiang’s camp and told his officers, “We are outnumbered and their earthworks are strong—a frontal contest will not serve; I must beat them by stratagem.”

sentences.zh: 」乃取數百雞以長繩連之，繫火於足。

translations.literal: He therefore took several hundred chickens, tied them with long cords, and fastened torches to their feet.
translations.idiomatic: He tied torches to hundreds of chickens on long cords.

sentences.zh: 群雞駭散，飛集襄營。

translations.literal: The flock panicked and scattered, flying into Xiang’s camp.
translations.idiomatic: The terrified birds bolted into Yao Xiang’s camp.

sentences.zh: 襄營火發，其亂，隨而擊之，襄遂小敗。

translations.literal: Fire broke out in Xiang’s camp; amid the confusion You attacked and Xiang suffered a minor defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Flames erupted in the enemy camp; You charged into the chaos and handed Yao Xiang a partial defeat.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫奏廢浩佐吏，遂免。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen memorialized to dismiss Hao’s aides You was therefore removed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen purged Yin Hao’s staff and You lost his post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除中書郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became a gentleman of the palace writers.

sentences.zh: 升平中，遷吏部郎，長兼侍中。

translations.literal: During the Shengping era he rose to gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shengping he advanced to the Ministry of Personnel and served concurrently as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 穆帝將修後池，起閣道，逌上疏曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Mu was about to renovate the rear pond and build a gallery bridge; You submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mu planned to enlarge the rear pond and raise a covered walkway You addressed the throne:

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其言而止。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and dropped the project.

sentences.zh: 復領本州大中正。

translations.literal: He again headed his province’s senior locator.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed duty as senior locator for his home province.

sentences.zh: 升平末，遷太常，逌累讓，不許。

translations.literal: Late in Shengping he was transferred to Chamberlain for Ceremonial; You repeatedly declined but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shengping he became chamberlain for ceremonial rites—he tried to refuse repeatedly but the court insisted.

sentences.zh: 穆帝崩，山陵將用寶器，諫曰：「以宣皇顧命終制，山陵不設明器，以貽後則。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu died the imperial tomb was to employ precious grave goods; You remonstrated: “According to Emperor Xuan’s testamentary compact the mound must set out no bright vessels so as to hand down a model.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Mu died ministers wanted rich tomb goods; You argued that Emperor Xuan’s dying instructions forbade lavish grave offerings meant to set precedent.

sentences.zh: 景帝奉遵遺制。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing followed the bequest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing obeyed that legacy.

sentences.zh: 逮文明皇后崩，武皇帝亦承前制，無所施設，惟脯脩之奠，瓦器而已。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenming died Emperor Wu likewise continued prior models, setting out nothing except dried-meat offerings and earthen vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenming passed away Emperor Wu likewise kept things austere—only dried meat and pottery vessels at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 昔康皇帝玄宮始用寶劍金舄，此蓋太妃罔已之情，實違先旨累世之法。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Kang’s underground palace first used precious swords and gold slippers—this stemmed from the grand consort’s unbearable grief yet violated ancestral intent and generations of law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang’s burial first introduced jeweled blades and gold slippers—emotion overrode precedent and broke generations of restraint.

sentences.zh: 今外欲以為故事，臣請述先旨，停此二物。

translations.literal: Now those outside wish to treat it as precedent; I beg to rehearse prior intent and halt these two kinds of object.
translations.idiomatic: Now officials want that excess as routine—You asked to reaffirm older restraint and ban both items.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 哀帝以天文失度，欲依《尚書》洪祀之制，於太極前殿親執虔肅，冀以免咎，使太常集博士草其制。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai, because celestial patterns were awry, wished to follow the Hong sacrifice protocol in the Documents at the forward hall of the Supreme Ultimate, personally maintaining reverent vigil in hope of averting blame; he ordered the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to gather erudits and draft the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai blamed heaven’s omens and wanted the Hong sacrifice from the 《Documents》 performed in the Taiji Hall—he would stand vigil himself—and told the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to draft rites with the boshi scholars.

sentences.zh: 逌上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: You submitted a memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: You filed a counter-memorial:

sentences.zh: 帝不納，逌又上疏曰：

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it; You submitted again:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed him off; You wrote again:

sentences.zh: 帝猶敕撰定，逌又陳古義，帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor still ordered compilation; You again presented classical precedents, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still pressed for a codified rite until You cited classical precedent again and he gave up.

sentences.zh: 逌在職多所匡諫。

translations.literal: While in office You often corrected and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his tenure he remonstrated freely.

sentences.zh: 著《阮籍序贊》、《逸士箴》及詩賦奏議數十篇行於世。

translations.literal: He authored “Preface and Encomium for Ruan Ji,” “Admonition for Recluses,” and several tens of poems, fu, and memorials that circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote essays such as 《Preface and Encomium for Ruan Ji》 and 《Admonition for Recluses》, plus dozens of poems, rhapsodies, and memorials that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 病卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: He died of illness at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子蔚，吳興太守。

translations.literal: His son Wei served as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang Wei governed Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 從弟灌

translations.literal: Younger cousin Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Guan, You’s younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 從弟灌

translations.literal: Younger cousin Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Guan.

sentences.zh: 灌字道群。

translations.literal: Guan, courtesy name Daoqun.
translations.idiomatic: Guan used the courtesy name Daoqun.

sentences.zh: 父瞢，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Meng had been a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng once served as a gentleman clerk in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 灌少知名，才識亞於逌。

translations.literal: Guan was known young; his talent and insight ranked just below You’s.
translations.idiomatic: Guan won notice early—second only to Jiang You in reputation.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，為治中，轉別駕，歷司徒屬、北中郎中長史，領晉陵太守。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk; he passed the provincial examination; he served as administrator of records, transferred to provincial aide, successively served as secretary under the minister of education, senior clerk to the north-center section chief, and concurrent Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from provincial recorder and aide to posts under the minister of education and chief clerk of the northern palace section, doubling as Jinling prefect.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝引為撫軍從事中郎，後遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen brought him in as attendant gentleman-in-chief on the pacification army staff; later he rose to gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen named him senior attendant on the pacification staff; he later joined the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時謝奕為尚書，銓敘不允，灌每執正不從，奕托以他事免之，受黜無怨色。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Yi was minister; personnel judgments were unfair; Guan often upheld rectitude and refused to comply; Yi found another excuse to dismiss him, yet he bore demotion without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Yi ran personnel assignments unfairly Guan held the line—Yi cashiered him on a pretext, but Guan accepted it without complaint.

sentences.zh: 頃之，簡文帝又以為撫軍司馬，甚相賓禮。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Jianwen again appointed him marshal of the pacification army and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Jianwen made him marshal of the pacification army and honored him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，轉吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace assistant censor and transferred to Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to imperial censor then prefect of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 灌性方正，視權貴蔑如也，為大司馬桓溫所惡。

translations.literal: Guan’s nature was upright; he treated mighty nobles with contempt and Grand Marshal Huan Wen loathed him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright to a fault, Guan snubbed power brokers—Huan Wen detested him.

sentences.zh: 溫欲中傷之，徵拜侍中，以在郡時公事有失，追免之。

translations.literal: Wen wished to ruin him: he summoned him as palace attendant and then, citing administrative faults while in commandery office, stripped him retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen tried to trap him—summoned him as palace attendant, then dredged up prefectural paperwork to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 後為秘書監，尋復解職。

translations.literal: Later he became secretary supervisor but soon resigned.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly headed the palace library then stepped down.

sentences.zh: 時溫方執權，朝廷希旨，故灌積年不調。

translations.literal: At that time Wen held power and the court followed his lead; therefore Guan went years without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: With Huan Wen dominating court appointments Guan languished without a new post.

sentences.zh: 溫末年，以為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In Wen’s last years he appointed him adviser on staff.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life Huan Wen relented and named him staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 會溫薨，遷尚書、中護軍，復出為吳郡太守，加秩中二千石，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: When Wen died Guan rose to minister and Defender of the Center, again went out as Administrator of Wu Commandery, was slated for salary of two thousand shi plus rank, but died before investiture.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen died Guan climbed to minister and Defender of the Center, returned as Wu prefect with top salary—and died before the seal arrived.

sentences.zh: 子績。

translations.literal: Son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His heir was Jiang Ji.

sentences.zh: 灌子績

translations.literal: Guan’s son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, Guan’s son.

sentences.zh: 灌子績

translations.literal: Guan’s son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji.

sentences.zh: 績字仲元，有志氣，除秘書郎。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Zhongyuan, had strong resolve and was appointed secretary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Ji bore the courtesy name Zhongyuan, showed backbone, and became a palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 以父與謝氏不穆，故謝安之世辟召無所從，論者多之。

translations.literal: Because his father was estranged from the Xie clan, during Xie An’s lifetime summoning orders never found acceptance—critics praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His father’s feud with the Xie meant Ji ignored every summons while Xie An lived—opinion admired his stance.

sentences.zh: 安薨，始為會稽王道子驃騎主簿，多所規諫。

translations.literal: After An died he first served Prince Kuaiji Daozi as chief clerk of the cavalry command and often remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xie An died he joined Prince Daozi of Kuaiji as cavalry chief clerk and spoke truth to power.

sentences.zh: 歷諮議參軍，出為南郡相。

translations.literal: He served as adviser on staff and went out as chancellor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He advised princes and then governed Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史殷仲堪舉兵以應王恭，仲堪要績與南蠻校尉殷顗同行，並不從。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Jing Yin Zhongkan raised troops to answer Wang Gong, Zhongkan pressed Ji to travel with Southern Man Colonel Yin Yi—both refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongkan mobilized to support Wang Gong he insisted Ji travel with Yin Yi—both men refused.

sentences.zh: 仲堪等屢以為言，績終不為之屈。

translations.literal: Zhongkan and others repeatedly pressed the point; Ji never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan kept demanding; Ji never bent.

sentences.zh: 顗慮績及禍，乃于仲堪坐和解之。

translations.literal: Yi feared Ji would court disaster and at Zhongkan’s banquet mediated.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yi feared bloodshed and mediated at Zhongkan’s banquet.

sentences.zh: 績曰：「大丈夫何至以死相脅！

translations.literal: Ji said: “How could a great man threaten another with death!”
translations.idiomatic: Ji snapped, “Must a gentleman threaten death?”

sentences.zh: 江仲元行年六十，但未知獲死所耳。

translations.literal: “Jiang Zhongyuan is sixty years old—I simply do not yet know where I shall die.”
translations.idiomatic: “Jiang Zhongyuan is sixty—I only wonder where I shall fall.”

sentences.zh: 」一坐為之懼。

translations.literal: The whole company feared on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The table fell silent in dread.

sentences.zh: 仲堪憚其堅正，以楊佺期代之。

translations.literal: Zhongkan dreaded his firm integrity and replaced him with Yang Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan, unnerved by his steel, swapped him for Yang Quanqi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而征績為御史中丞，奏劾無所屈撓。

translations.literal: The court heard and summoned Ji as palace assistant censor; his impeachments bowed to none.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as censor—his indictments showed no favor.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯專政，夜開六門，績密啟會稽王道子，欲以奏聞，道子不許。

translations.literal: The heir apparent of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, monopolized power, opening the six gates by night; Ji secretly informed Prince Daozi of Kuaiji wishing to memorialize; Daozi forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuanxian of Kuaiji seized power and opened the six palace gates at night Ji secretly urged Prince Daozi to report it—Daozi refused.

sentences.zh: 車胤亦曰：「元顯驕縱，宜禁制之。

translations.literal: Che Yin also said: “Yuanxian is arrogant and unrestrained; he should be restrained.”
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin added, “Yuanxian’s arrogance must be curbed.”

sentences.zh: 」道子默然。

translations.literal: Daozi was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi said nothing.

sentences.zh: 元顯聞而謂衆曰：「江績、車胤間我父子。

translations.literal: Yuanxian heard and told the assembly: “Jiang Ji and Che Yin drive a wedge between me and my father.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian heard and announced, “Jiang Ji and Che Yin are splitting my father and me.”

sentences.zh: 」遣人密讓之。

translations.literal: He sent men secretly to rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to reprimand them quietly.

sentences.zh: 俄而績卒，朝野悼之。

translations.literal: Soon Ji died; court and countryside mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji died soon after; capital and countryside mourned.

sentences.zh: 車胤

translations.literal: Che Yin
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin

sentences.zh: 車胤，字武子，南平人也。

translations.literal: Che Yin, courtesy name Wuzi, was a native of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin, courtesy Wuzi, hailed from Nanping.

sentences.zh: 曾祖浚，吳會稽太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jun had been Administrator of Kuaiji under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jun governed Kuaiji under Wu.

sentences.zh: 父育，郡主簿。

translations.literal: His father Yu had been county chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu served as county recorder.

sentences.zh: 太守王胡之名知人，見胤于童幼之中，謂胤父曰：「此兒當大興卿門，可使專學。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Huzhi was famed for judging men; seeing Yin among children he told Yin’s father: “This boy will greatly exalt your house—have him devote himself to study.”
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Huzhi sized him up in the schoolyard and told his father, “This child will glorify your line—let him study.”

sentences.zh: 」胤恭勤不倦，博學多通。

translations.literal: Yin was respectful and diligent without weariness; he was broadly learned and mastered many subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin studied tirelessly and mastered many disciplines.

sentences.zh: 家貧不常得油，夏月則練囊盛數十螢火以照書，以夜繼日焉。
