translations.literal: His household was poor and could not always obtain lamp oil; in summer he packed dozens of fireflies in a silk sack to illuminate his books, continuing day into night.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor for lamp oil, he stuffed fireflies in a silk bag to read by night—the famous “firefly glow” diligence.

sentences.zh: 及長，風姿美劭，機悟敏速，甚有鄉曲之譽。

translations.literal: When grown he was handsome and alert, quick and perceptive, and enjoyed great local renown.
translations.idiomatic: Grown handsome and sharp, he won wide local fame.

sentences.zh: 桓溫在荊州，辟為從事，以辯識義理深重之。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen was in Jing Province he summoned Yin as aide and deeply valued him for debating principles.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen in Jingzhou hired him as aide and prized his grasp of principle.

sentences.zh: 引為主簿，稍遷別駕、征西長史，遂顯於朝廷。

translations.literal: He brought him in as chief clerk and gradually promoted him to provincial aide and chief clerk of the western expedition; thus he became eminent at court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from chief clerk to provincial aide and western campaign chief clerk—then made his name at court.

sentences.zh: 時惟胤與吳隱之以寒素博學知名於世。

translations.literal: At the time only Yin and Wu Yinzhi were famed for humble origins yet broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Only Che Yin and Wu Yinzhi were celebrated for rising from cold households through scholarship.

sentences.zh: 又善於賞會，當時每有盛坐而胤不在，皆云：「無車公不樂。

translations.literal: He also excelled at hosting gatherings; whenever there was a splendid banquet without Yin, all said, “Without Lord Che there is no joy.”
translations.idiomatic: He hosted surpassingly well—guests swore no feast sparkled without “Lord Che.”

sentences.zh: 」謝安遊集之日，輒開筵待之。

translations.literal: Whenever Xie An held outings he always spread a feast and awaited him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xie An entertained he saved a seat for Che Yin.

sentences.zh: 甯康初，以胤為中書侍郎、關內侯。

translations.literal: In the early Ningkang era Yin was appointed gentleman of the palace secretariat and marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ningkang he became palace secretary and marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝嘗講《孝經》，僕射謝安侍坐，尚書陸納侍講，侍中卞眈執讀，黃門侍郎謝石、吏部郎袁宏執經，胤與丹陽尹王混擿句，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety: Vice Director Xie An sat in attendance, Minister Lu Na attended the exposition, Palace Attendant Bian Dan held the text, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Xie Shi and Gentleman in Personnel Yuan Hong held the classics, while Yin and Prefect of Danyang Wang Hun parsed lines—opinion of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu expounded the 《Classic of Filial Piety》, Xie An, Lu Na, Bian Dan, Xie Shi, Yuan Hong, Che Yin, and Wang Hun each played a ceremonial role—the age deemed it glory.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced stepwise to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 太元中，增置太學生百人，以胤領國子博士。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan era they added a hundred National Academy students and placed Yin in charge as libationer doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiyuan the academy added a hundred students and named Yin their doctoral libationer.

sentences.zh: 其後年，議郊廟明堂之事，胤以「明堂之制既甚難詳，且樂主於和，禮主於敬，故質文不同，音器亦殊。

translations.literal: The following year, debating suburban altars and the Bright Hall, Yin argued that “the Bright Hall system is already hard to pin down, and since music aims at harmony while ritual aims at reverence, substance and ornament differ and therefore tones and vessels diverge.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, arguing suburban rites and the Bright Hall, Che Yin began: “Bright Hall layout is notoriously elusive; music pursues harmony, ritual pursues reverence, so form and ornament diverge and bells and vessels cannot match.”

sentences.zh: 既茅茨廣廈不一其度，何必守其形範而不弘本順時乎！

translations.literal: Since thatched huts and grand halls do not share one measure, why cling to mere outward models instead of honoring the root and following the season?
translations.idiomatic: Thatched cottages and marble halls follow different scales—why fetishize shape rather than grasp the essence and move with the times?

sentences.zh: 九服咸寧，四野無塵，然後明堂辟雍可光而修之。

translations.literal: Only when the nine circuits are calm and the four wildernesses bear no dust may one gloriously restore the Bright Hall and Biyong.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the realm is quiet and dust-free across the frontiers—then you may splendidly rebuild Bright Hall and the royal academy.

sentences.zh: 」時從其議。

translations.literal: At the time the court followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 又遷驃騎長史、太常，進爵臨湘侯，以疾去職。

translations.literal: He was further promoted chief clerk of the chariot-and-cavalry command and Chamberlain for Ceremonial, advanced to Marquis of Linxiang, then left office owing to illness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to cavalry chief clerk and chamberlain for rites, became marquis of Linxiang, then resigned ill.

sentences.zh: 俄為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he served as Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded the Defender-in-Chief army.

sentences.zh: 時王國寶諂于會稽王道子，諷八坐啟以道子為丞相，加殊禮。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Guobao flattered Prince Daozi of Kuaiji and prompted the Eight Seats to memorialize making Daozi chancellor with extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao curried favor with Prince Daozi of Kuaiji and coached the Eight Seats to ask that Daozi become chancellor with superlative ceremony.

sentences.zh: 胤曰：「此乃成王所以尊周公也。

translations.literal: Yin said: “That is how the youthful king honored the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin replied, “Such honors fit how the young king deferred to the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今主上當陽，非成王之地，相王在位，豈得為周公乎！

translations.literal: Now the sovereign faces south—this is not the youthful king’s situation—and the prince regent holds office—how can he equal the Duke of Zhou!”
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor sits openly on the throne—not a minor regency—and the prince regent is no Duke of Zhou.”

sentences.zh: 望實二三，並不宜爾，必大忤上意。

translations.literal: Their reputations fall short two or threefold in both deed and reality—none of this fits and will surely deeply offend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Neither prestige nor substance warrants this—it will only insult the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」乃稱疾不署其事。

translations.literal: He therefore pleaded illness and refused to endorse the document.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned sickness and withheld his signature.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝大怒，而甚嘉胤。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor was furious yet deeply praised Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged at the proposal but applauded Che Yin.

sentences.zh: 隆安初，為吳興太守，秩中二千石，辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: In the early Longan era he was appointed Administrator of Wuxing at salary of two thousand shi—he declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longan they named him Wuxing prefect at top salary—he pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 加輔國將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was additionally General Who Supports the State and Prefect of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: They added titles as supporting-state general and Danyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he rose to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元顯有過，胤與江績密言于道子，將奏之，事泄，元顯逼令自裁。

translations.literal: Yuanxian erred; Yin and Jiang Ji spoke secretly to Daozi planning to memorialize; the affair leaked and Yuanxian forced him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanxian misbehaved Che Yin and Jiang Ji whispered to Daozi about impeachment—word slipped out and Yuanxian drove Che Yin to suicide.

sentences.zh: 俄而胤卒，朝廷傷之。

translations.literal: Soon Yin died and the court mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin died shortly after; the court grieved.

sentences.zh: 殷顗

translations.literal: Yin Yi
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yi

sentences.zh: 殷顗，字伯通，陳郡人也。

translations.literal: Yin Yi, courtesy name Botong, was a native of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yi, courtesy Botong, came from Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖融，太常卿。

translations.literal: His ancestor Rong had been Chamberlain for Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yin Rong led the Chamberlain’s office.

sentences.zh: 父康，吳興太守。

translations.literal: His father Kang had been Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang governed Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 顗性通率，有才氣，少與從弟仲堪俱知名。

translations.literal: Yi was frank and generous by nature, talented, and in youth shared fame with his cousin Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was open-hearted and gifted—celebrated alongside cousin Yin Zhongkan in youth.

sentences.zh: 太元中，以中書郎擢為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan era he rose from gentleman of the palace secretariat to Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taiyuan he jumped from palace secretary to southern tribes colonel.

sentences.zh: 蒞職清明，政績肅舉。

translations.literal: His tenure was lucid and his administration sternly effective.
translations.idiomatic: His rule stayed clean and crisp.

sentences.zh: 及仲堪得王恭書，將興兵內伐，告顗，欲同舉。

translations.literal: When Zhongkan received Wang Gong’s letter and planned to raise troops inward against the court he informed Yi and wished to act together.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongkan got Wang Gong’s letter plotting an attack on the capital he told Yi and wanted joint action.

sentences.zh: 顗不平之，曰：「夫人臣之義，慎保所守。

translations.literal: Yi was displeased and said: “The duty of a minister is carefully to guard what he holds.
translations.idiomatic: Yi bridled: “Ministers must guard their posts.

sentences.zh: 朝廷是非，宰輔之務，豈籓屏之所圖也。

translations.literal: Right and wrong at court are the chief ministers’ business—how can a screen prince scheme them?
translations.idiomatic: Court disputes belong to the chief ministers—not frontier intendants.

sentences.zh: 晉陽之事，宜所不豫。

translations.literal: Affairs like the Jinyang expedition are not what you should join.
translations.idiomatic: “Jinyang-style” coups are none of your business.

sentences.zh: 」仲堪要之轉切，顗怒曰：「吾進不敢同，退不敢異。

translations.literal: Zhongkan pressed harder; Yi angrily said: “Advancing I dare not join you; retreating I dare not oppose you.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan doubled down; Yi snapped, “I will neither march with you nor scheme against you.”

sentences.zh: 」仲堪以為恨。

translations.literal: Zhongkan nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 猶密諫仲堪，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: Yi still secretly remonstrated Zhongkan with utmost earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi still slipped Zhongkan urgent secret warnings.

sentences.zh: 仲堪既貴，素情亦殊，而志望無厭，謂顗言為非。

translations.literal: Once Zhongkan grew powerful his temperament changed and ambition knew no satiety; he deemed Yi’s words wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Power changed Zhongkan—his appetite grew and he dismissed Yi’s counsel.

sentences.zh: 顗見江績亦以正直為仲堪所斥，知仲堪當逐異己，樹置所親，因出行散，托疾不還。

translations.literal: Seeing Jiang Ji likewise expelled for integrity, Yi knew Zhongkan would purge dissenters and plant favorites; he therefore went out to take walking powder, pleaded illness, and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Watching Jiang Ji cashiered for honesty Yi knew Zhongkan would purge outsiders—he left on “walking powder,” claimed illness, and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 仲堪聞其病，出省之，謂顗曰：「兄病殊為可憂。

translations.literal: Zhongkan heard of his illness and went out to console him, telling Yi: “Elder brother, your illness truly worries me.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan visited his sickbed and said, “Brother, this sickness frightens me.”

sentences.zh: 」顗曰：「我病不過身死，但汝病在滅門，幸熟為慮，勿以我為念也。

translations.literal: Yi said: “My sickness goes no further than my death, but yours threatens your entire clan—think hard and do not fret over me.”
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered, “My worst is death; yours is clan extinction—think about yourself, not me.”

sentences.zh: 」仲堪不從，卒與楊佺期、桓玄同下。

translations.literal: Zhongkan did not listen and ultimately descended east with Yang Quanqi and Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan ignored him and marched east with Yang Quanqi and Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 顗遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: Yi therefore died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yi died of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，詔曰：「故南蠻校尉殷顗忠績未融，奄焉隕喪，可贈冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In mid Longan an edict stated: “The late Colonel of the Southern Man Yin Yi’s loyal merit never ripened before he suddenly passed—posthumously appoint him General Who Champions the Army.”
translations.idiomatic: A Longan edict mourned Colonel Yin Yi—loyalty cut short—and posthumously named him champion general.

sentences.zh: 」弟仲文、叔獻別有傳。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Zhongwen and Shuxian have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Yin Zhongwen and Yin Shuxian appear elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 王雅

translations.literal: Wang Ya
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya

sentences.zh: 王雅，字茂達，東海郯人，魏衛將軍肅之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Ya, courtesy name Maoda, was a native of Tan in Donghai and great-grandson of Wei General Who Guards the Right Wang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, courtesy Maoda, came from Tan in Donghai—descended from Wang Su, Wei’s guard-general of the right.

sentences.zh: 祖隆，後將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Long had been General of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Long commanded the rear army.

sentences.zh: 父景，大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Jing had been Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 雅少知名，州檄主簿，舉秀才，除郎中，出補永興令，以幹理著稱。

translations.literal: Ya was known young; the province summoned him chief clerk; he passed the examination; he was appointed gentleman; went out as magistrate of Yongxing— famed for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya rose early—provincial aide, examination graduate, gentleman, Yongxing magistrate—with a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左右丞，歷廷尉、侍中、左衛將軍、丹陽尹，領太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Left and Right Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing, served as commandant of justice, palace attendant, General Who Guards the Left, Prefect of Danyang, and concurrently commanded the heir’s left guard.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to assistant ministers of the secretariat, commandant of justice, palace attendant, general guarding the left, Danyang prefect, plus commander of the heir’s left guard.

sentences.zh: 雅性好接下，敬慎奉公，孝武帝深加禮遇，雖在外職，侍見甚數，朝廷大事多參謀議。

translations.literal: Ya loved receiving inferiors; he was reverent and cautious in public service; Emperor Xiaowu deeply favored him—although holding outside posts he was summoned often and participated widely in great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya welcomed junior officers, served carefully, and enjoyed Emperor Xiaowu’s trust—despite outside duties he advised constantly on state matters.

sentences.zh: 帝每置酒宴集，雅未至，不先舉觴，其見重如此。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor held banquets he would not lift his cup until Ya arrived—such was the esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet the emperor waited for Wang Ya before drinking—such was his standing.

sentences.zh: 然任遇有過其才，時人被以佞幸之目。

translations.literal: Yet favor exceeded his talent; contemporaries labeled him sycophantic.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rewards outstripped ability—critics called him a court favorite.

sentences.zh: 帝起清暑殿于後宮，開北上閣，出華林園，與美人張氏同遊止，惟雅與焉。

translations.literal: The emperor built the Cool Summer Palace in the rear palace, opened the northern upper gate to exit Hualin Garden, and roamed and lodged with the beauty Lady Zhang—only Ya accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built Cool Summer Palace, opened a back gate into Hualin Garden, and toured with Lady Zhang—only Wang Ya joined.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子領太子太傅，以雅為太子少傅。

translations.literal: Prince Daozi of Kuaiji headed the heir’s grand tutorate and appointed Ya Junior Tutor to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi of Kuaiji led the heir’s tutorship and named Wang Ya junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 時王珣兒婚，賓客車騎甚衆，會聞雅拜少傅，回詣雅者過半。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xun’s son married; guests and carriages thronged—when word spread that Ya had been named junior tutor more than half turned back to visit Ya.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Xun’s son’s wedding crowds jammed the roads—but half wheeled away once Wang Ya’s junior tutor appointment broke.

sentences.zh: 時風俗頹弊，無復廉恥。

translations.literal: Custom was decadent beyond shame.
translations.idiomatic: Manners had rotted beyond embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 然少傅之任，朝望屬珣，珣亦頗以自幸。

translations.literal: Yet court expectation had pinned the junior tutor post on Xun, and Xun himself rather fancied the honor.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone had expected Wang Xun to win the post—and Xun counted on it.

sentences.zh: 及中詔用雅，衆遂赴雅焉。

translations.literal: When the palace edict chose Ya the multitude flocked to Ya instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict picked Wang Ya the crowd rushed to him.

sentences.zh: 將拜，遇雨，請以傘入。

translations.literal: About to be invested, rain fell; he requested to enter with an umbrella.
translations.idiomatic: Rain soaked investiture day; he asked to carry an umbrella indoors.

sentences.zh: 王珣不許之，因冒雨而拜。

translations.literal: Wang Xun forbade it, so he underwent investiture through the rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun refused—Wang Ya took the ritual soaked to the skin.

sentences.zh: 雅既貴幸，威權甚震，門下車騎常數百，而善應接，傾心禮之。

translations.literal: Once Ya grew favored his authority awed others—hundreds of carriages filled his gate—yet he courteously received everyone who sought him.
translations.idiomatic: Power swelled his salon to hundreds of carriages—yet he greeted each petitioner graciously.

sentences.zh: 帝以道子無社稷器幹，慮晏駕之後皇室傾危，乃選時望以為籓屏，將擢王恭、殷仲堪等，先以訪雅。

translations.literal: Because Daozi lacked capacity to shoulder the altars the emperor feared peril to the house after his death; he therefore chose leading reputations as bulwarks and planned to elevate Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan—first he consulted Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Prince Daozi too weak to guard the dynasty, Emperor Xiaowu picked reputable buffers—Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan—and asked Wang Ya first.

sentences.zh: 雅以恭等無當世之才，不可大任，從容曰：「王恭風神簡貴，志氣方嚴，既居外戚之重，當親賢之寄，然其稟性峻隘，無所苞容，執自是之操，無守節之志。

translations.literal: Ya judged Gong and others lacking talent for the age and unsuited to heavy duty; calmly he said: “Wang Gong’s bearing is refined and lofty, his resolve stern—already burdened as maternal kin and entrusted as intimate—yet his nature is narrow and admits no breadth; he clings to self-righteousness and lacks constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya thought them unfit: “Wang Gong looks noble and acts severe—as imperial in-law he shoulders heavy trust—yet he is cramped, unforgiving, stubborn, and unreliable.

sentences.zh: 仲堪雖謹於細行，以文義著稱，亦無弘量，且幹略不長。

translations.literal: Zhongkan, though meticulous in small conduct and famed for literary taste, likewise lacks breadth and moreover short strategic grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan fusses petty detail and literary fame yet lacks breadth or strategic depth.

sentences.zh: 若委以連率之重，據形勝之地，今四海無事，足能守職，若道不常隆，必為亂階矣。

translations.literal: If you entrust them with governor-general weight and strategic terrain, while the realm is calm they may suffice—but if the Way does not remain prosperous they will become seeds of rebellion.”
translations.idiomatic: Give them frontier supremacy while peace lasts they might cope—if fortune falters they become rebellion itself.”

sentences.zh: 」帝以恭等為當時秀望，謂雅疾其勝己，故不從。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed Gong and others the leading talents of the moment and supposed Ya envied their superiority—therefore he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Wang Gong’s circle the best of the age and assumed Wang Ya jealous—so he ignored him.

sentences.zh: 二人皆被升用，其後竟敗，有識之士稱其知人。

translations.literal: Both men were promoted and afterward indeed failed—knowing observers praised his judgment of men.
translations.idiomatic: Both rose—and later fell—while wise men credited Wang Ya’s insight.

sentences.zh: 遷領軍、尚書、散騎常侍，方大崇進之，將參副相之重，而帝崩，倉卒不獲顧命。

translations.literal: He rose to command the armies, minister, gentleman at the palace gate—great advancement was planned with deputy chief minister rank—then the emperor died and hasty circumstances denied a testament.
translations.idiomatic: He neared minister and defender posts—then the emperor died suddenly without naming him regent.

sentences.zh: 雅素被優遇，一旦失權，又以朝廷方亂，內外攜離，但慎默而已，無所辯正。

translations.literal: Ya had long enjoyed favor; once power vanished and court turmoil tore inside from outside he kept cautious silence and corrected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Long favored, Wang Ya lost leverage overnight as chaos split court—he stayed mute.

sentences.zh: 雖在孝武世，亦不能犯顏廷爭，凡所謀謨，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: Even under Emperor Xiaowu he had not dared argue face to face at court; every stratagem he merely assented to.
translations.idiomatic: Even under Xiaowu he rarely debated openly—always nodding yes.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he rose to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became left vice director.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年六十七。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor, Unequaled in Honor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously named grand master of brilliant splendor with honors matching the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 長子准之，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Eldest son Zhunzhi, Gentleman for Palace Presentation.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest Zhunzhi served as palace presenter.

sentences.zh: 次協之，黃門。

translations.literal: Second Xiezhi, Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Xiezhi worked the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 次少卿，侍中。

translations.literal: Third Shaoqing, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Third son Shaoqing became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 並有士操，立名於世云。

translations.literal: All possessed gentlemen’s conduct and established names in the world.
translations.idiomatic: All kept gentlemanly reputations.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians’ appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historians’ commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：爰在中興，玄風滋扇，溺王綱於拱默，撓國步於清虛，骨鯁蹇諤之風蓋亦微矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: At the eastern restoration abstruse winds blew stronger—drowning royal norms in idle silence, stumbling the state march in empty purity—forthright remonstrance grew scarce indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Under the restored court “dark learning” numbed government—honest criticism nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 而君孝固情禮而違顯命，山甫獻誠讜而振頹風，彥叔之兵謀，道載之正諫，洋洋盈耳，有足可稱。

translations.literal: Yet Junxiao clung to feeling and ritual against shining mandates; Shanfu offered sincere counsel to revive a decadent wind; Yanshu’s military schemes and Daozai’s upright remonstrance ring richly—worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Still Gu He defied summons for mourning’s sake; Yuan Mei stirred Confucian schools; Yuan Qiao planned campaigns; Jiang You spoke plain truth—all merit praise.

sentences.zh: 灌不屈節於權臣，績敢危言於賊將，道子殊物之禮，車胤沮之無懼心，仲堪反常之舉，殷顗折之以正色，求諸古烈，何以加焉！

translations.literal: Guan bent no knee to power brokers; Ji dared bold words to rebel generals; Daozi’s extraordinary honors Che Yin blocked without fear; Zhongkan’s irregular plots Yin Yi broke with stern integrity—set beside ancient paragons, what could surpass them?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Guan refused cronies; Jiang Ji defied warlords; Che Yin thwarted Daozi’s excess; Yin Yi stared down Zhongkan—few ancients outdid them.

sentences.zh: 山松悅哀挽於軒冕之辰，彥道歡博徒於衰絰之日，天心已喪，其能濟乎！

translations.literal: Shansong took pleasure in laments amid court finery; Yandao reveled with gamblers while wearing mourning—heaven’s mind already lost—how could they prosper!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shansong sang dirges in silk hats; Yuan Dan diced in mourning clothes—hearts were dead—how expect salvation?

sentences.zh: 旋及於促齡，俄致於非命，宜哉！

translations.literal: Soon they met early death or violent ends—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: They died young or violently—justice enough.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：顧生軌物，屢申誠讜。

translations.literal: Encomium: Master Gu regulated conduct and repeatedly voiced sincere counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Verse praise: Gu He set standards and spoke truth.

sentences.zh: 袁子崇儒，拯斯頹喪。

translations.literal: Master Yuan upheld Confucian learning and rescued that decadent wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mei upheld Confucius against collapse.

sentences.zh: 逌績剛蹇，車殷忠壯。

translations.literal: You and Ji were rigidly upright; Che and Yin loyal and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You and Jiang Ji stood firm; Che Yin and Yin Yi showed courage.

sentences.zh: 睠言遺直，莫之能尚。

translations.literal: Turning to these lingering exemplars, none can surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering such upright survivors, none rank higher.
